title: IF / ELSIF -- Tank Pump with Real Analog Input
concept:
Conditional logic uses IF / ELSIF / ELSE / END_IF. Watch the spelling:
ELSIF (one E), END_IF, and a semicolon after END_IF;.

    IF condition THEN
        (* statements *)
    ELSIF other_condition THEN
        (* statements *)
    END_IF;

Comparisons:  =  <>  <  >  <=  >=   ('not equal' is <> ).

Real-world context: Tank_Level is a REAL from a level transmitter (e.g. a
4-20 mA submersible or radar sensor) scaled to 0.0-100.0 % in the analog input
module. Two setpoints (fill below 20 %, stop above 80 %) create a hysteresis
band so the pump motor doesn't short-cycle -- rapid start/stop that burns out
contactors and motors.
ab_note:
In Studio 5000 the raw analog count is scaled (module engineering units or an
SCL/CPT instruction) to give Tank_Level as a REAL. The IF/ELSIF then drives
Pump_Run. In practice you'd also AND in a Pump_OL overload and permissives
before energizing the pump output.
siemens_note:
SCL is identical: IF / ELSIF / ELSE / END_IF;. The analog channel is scaled
(NORM_X + SCALE_X) into a REAL level tag, then compared to the setpoints.
task:
Given Tank_Level : REAL (0-100 %) from the level transmitter and Pump_Run :
BOOL (pump contactor output), write an IF statement that:

    - Turns the pump ON  (Pump_Run := TRUE)  when Tank_Level < 20.0
    - Turns the pump OFF (Pump_Run := FALSE) when Tank_Level > 80.0
    - Leaves it unchanged between 20 and 80 (the hysteresis band)

Use IF ... ELSIF ... END_IF; -- no ELSE needed.
starter:
(* Lesson 03 -- IF / ELSIF: Tank Pump from a Real Analog Level *)

VAR
    Tank_Level : REAL;   (* 0.0-100.0 % from the level transmitter (analog input) *)
    Pump_Run   : BOOL;   (* pump contactor (output)                              *)
END_VAR

(* ----- YOUR LOGIC : write your answer between these two lines ----- *)
    (* TODO: pump ON below 20.0 %, OFF above 80.0 %, hold its state in between (hysteresis). *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)

checks.message: Uses ELSIF for the second setpoint
checks.hint: Second test:  ELSIF Tank_Level > 80.0 THEN  (ELSIF, one E).

checks.message: Turns the pump on with Pump_Run := TRUE
Turns the pump off with Pump_Run := FALSE
Executed: pump ON below 20, OFF above 80, unchanged in the band
checks.hint: Below 20 -> TRUE, above 80 -> FALSE, and leave Pump_Run unchanged between.

solution:
(* Lesson 03 -- IF / ELSIF: Tank Pump from a Real Analog Level *)

VAR
    Tank_Level : REAL;   (* 0.0-100.0 % from the level transmitter (analog input) *)
    Pump_Run   : BOOL;   (* pump contactor (output)                              *)
END_VAR

(* ----- YOUR LOGIC : write your answer between these two lines ----- *)
IF Tank_Level < 20.0 THEN
    Pump_Run := TRUE;
ELSIF Tank_Level > 80.0 THEN
    Pump_Run := FALSE;
END_IF;
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)
